original_value: Survey-grade Lidar brands have commercialized Lidar-based mobile mapping systems (MMSs) for several years now. With this high-end equipment, the high-level accuracy quality of point clouds can be ensured, but unfortunately, their high cost has prevented practical implementation in autonomous driving from being affordable. As an attempt to solve this problem, we present a cost-effective MMS to generate an accurate 3D color point cloud for autonomous vehicles. Among the major processes for color point cloud reconstruction, we first synchronize the timestamps of each sensor. The calibration process between camera and Lidar is developed to obtain the translation and rotation matrices, based on which color attributes can be composed into the corresponding Lidar points. We also employ control points to adjust the point cloud for fine tuning the absolute position. To overcome the limitation of Global Navigation Satellite System/Inertial Measurement Unit (GNSS/IMU) positioning system, we utilize Normal Distribution Transform (NDT) localization to refine the trajectory to solve the multi-scan dispersion issue. Experimental results show that the color point cloud reconstructed by the proposed MMS has a position error in centimeter-level accuracy, meeting the requirement of high definition (HD) maps for autonomous driving usage.

result.paraphrase: Survey-grade lidar vendors have been offering lidar-based mobile mapping systems (MMSs) for several years. This high-end equipment can deliver highly accurate point clouds, but its steep cost has kept practical use in autonomous driving from being affordable. To address this issue, we propose a low-cost MMS for generating accurate 3D color point clouds for autonomous vehicles. In the main steps of color point cloud reconstruction, we first align the timestamps of all sensors. We then develop a camera–lidar calibration method to obtain the translation and rotation matrices, which are used to assign color attributes to the corresponding lidar points. Control points are also used to fine-tune the absolute position of the point cloud. To mitigate the limitations of the Global Navigation Satellite System/Inertial Measurement Unit (GNSS/IMU) positioning system, we use Normal Distribution Transform (NDT) localization to refine the trajectory and resolve the multi-scan dispersion problem. Experimental results indicate that the reconstructed color point cloud from the proposed MMS achieves centimeter-level position error, satisfying the requirements of high-definition (HD) maps for autonomous driving.
